question.text: Mr. Arjun Mehta, fixed-income head at Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III), quotes the 1-year sovereign yield at 7.30% and the consensus 1-year CPI expectation at 5.10%. Using the Fisher decomposition as stated in NISM Section 1.4.1, what is the IMPLIED real risk-free rate (rounded to 2 decimal places)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 1.4.1 gives Nominal = (1 + Real) x (1 + Inflation) - 1. Inverting: (1 + Real) = (1 + 0.0730) / (1 + 0.0510) = 1.0730 / 1.0510 = 1.02093... So Real ≈ 2.09%. Option A (2.20%) is the simplistic Nominal - Inflation = 7.30 - 5.10 subtraction which IGNORES the cross-product term and is an approximation, not the Fisher equation. Option C adds instead of divides. Option D uses wrong base. The Trap: Option A is the #1 trap — candidates who learned 'Real = Nominal - Inflation' flat subtract and get 2.20%. The NISM chapter's Example box explicitly uses the MULTIPLICATIVE Fisher form [(1+Real)(1+Inflation) - 1], which at higher inflation rates diverges measurably from simple subtraction. Cross-Exam Context: XV (Research Analyst), XXI-B (Portfolio Manager), X-B (IA L2) all test Fisher decomposition. XIX-E frames it at the macro-desk level — real-rate estimation drives Cat III global-macro positioning in sovereign curves, gold and INR.
